title: Multi-Regional Conversational Streaming SLO & Per-Customer Error Budget Policy
creator: Priya Rao
description: PRD excerpt: Define operational SLOs for low-latency conversational streaming across multiple regions and establish a per-customer error budget policy that enables progressive rollouts and automated fallback when budgets deplete. Scope includes: (1) SLO targets for first-token and per-token latency for streaming chat paths, (2) availability targets for region-local endpoints with cross-region fallback behavior, (3) error budget accounting at tenant and global levels (rolling 30-day window), and (4) rollout gates with automated throttles and model fallbacks tied to budget burn. Excludes: billing changes and Dedicated-only capacity knobs (handled in separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: SLO table defined and approved with p50/p95/p99 latency bands for first-token and steady-state per-token delivery across supported regions
Availability SLOs and decomposed regional targets documented (regional availability, cross-region failover latency budget)
Error budget calculation method specified for per-customer and global budgets (rolling 30-day window) and edge cases (clock skew, replayed requests)
Rollout gate rules expressed as automatable thresholds (e.g., 7-day burn rate > 2x -> throttle to 50%) and mapped to Console controls
Test plan for canary and staged rollouts with synthetic and real traffic has pass/fail criteria and runbooks
Dashboard and alerting spec created (SLO burn, per-tenant burn, long tail latency regressions) with owners assigned
Product, Eng, and Security sign-off recorded in comments and PRD links
rollout_gates: Canary: 1% traffic -> hold for 24h with no more than 10% of expected error budget consumed
Stage 1: 10% traffic -> require <1.5x expected 7-day burn rate and p95 latency within target for 48h
Stage 2: 50% traffic -> require <1.2x 7-day burn rate and per-tenant burn thresholds not exceeded for any tenant >1% traffic
Full: 100% traffic -> automatic promotion if 14-day burn rate within expected bounds; otherwise rollback to previous model or enable degraded routing
Automated fallback: if regional availability < SLO or per-tenant budget depleted -> route to compatible lower-cost quantized model or alternate region based on routing policy
metrics: Per-token steady-state SLOs: p50 < 15ms, p95 < 50ms, p99 < 150ms
Error budget: global 0.05% availability allowance (30-day window); per-customer budgets proportional to traffic share, min budget floor for low-volume tenants
Burn-rate alarm thresholds: 7-day burn rate > 2x -> page on-call; >3x -> automatic throttle to 50% of new sessions
test_plan: Build synthetic streaming harness to measure first-token and per-token latencies across regions under representative load
Run canary with synthetic traffic in a dedicated namespace for 24h and compare against control model
Staged rollout against sampled real traffic with per-tenant monitoring enabled (enable feature flag to cap per-tenant exposure)
Introduce simulated region outage to verify cross-region failover and SLO accounting consistency
Execute chaos test where certain tenants have sudden spike to validate per-customer budget enforcement and throttling behavior
notes: Trade-offs: strict per-tenant budgets protect noisy neighbors but add complexity to routing and billing reconciliation. Proposed compromise: enforce soft-safeguards for small tenants and hard-safeguards for tenants >1% traffic.
Decision: prefer model fallback to global rollback whenever possible to reduce blast radius; fallback models must be declared compatible in model catalog.
Open question: whether to surface per-tenant remaining budget to customers in Console (UX dependency) — leaning yes, tracked in follow-up PM ticket.
Risk: clock skew across regions will affect rolling-window accounting; ENG to provide mitigation (time-sync normalization) in ENG-39122.
